clue.text: Dress up in these for cheerful student pranks

parts.note: cheerful means glad
rags are the stunts and pranks of British student charity weeks

explanation.surface: Students dress up for their cheerful charity-week stunts.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAG is a British university charity event full of pranks; 'glad rags' are one's best clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags are smart party clothes, the outfit you put on when dressing up.

clue.text: Two types of suit for this athletic event

parts.note: a long suit is a bridge holding of many cards in one suit
a jumpsuit is a one-piece garment

explanation.surface: Two kinds of outfit for a sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' works two ways: LONG from a bridge player's long suit, JUMP from a jumpsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The long jump is a track-and-field contest of leaping distance from a run-up.

clue.text: Record playing so lifeless, it's very sad

parts.note: a record is a disc
a record playing is on
late means dead, lifeless

explanation.surface: A record played so dully that it is depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' as in 'the late king' means dead, hence lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disconsolate is utterly dejected and cannot be comforted.

clue.text: Disposal of a river barrier? Water's the result

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across a river
a sale disposes of goods

explanation.surface: What happens when a river dam is sold off? Water floods out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adam's ale' is a jocular old name for plain water, the only drink Adam had.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a humorous idiom for drinking water.

clue.text: Unexplored way over the mountains

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a range is a chain of mountains, read here simply as mountains with over as a link

explanation.surface: An uncharted route across a mountain chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Unexplored territory is unfamiliar, new and unknown to the traveller.

clue.text: Maker of snap judgments given privately here

definitions.text: Maker of snap judgments given privately here

parts.words: Maker of snap judgments given privately here
parts.note: a device that takes snapshots, and also the legal phrase 'in ...' for court hearings held in private chambers

explanation.surface: A place where hasty verdicts are delivered behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap judgments' looks like a phrase about hasty decisions; split it into snap (a photo) and judgments given in private, which are made 'in camera'.
explanation.definitionFit: The device takes snaps, and a court sitting privately is said to sit in camera.

clue.text: Entertain a large crowd

definitions.meaning: to act as the person welcoming guests
a multitude, a great number of people

explanation.definitionFit: To be the person giving a party is to entertain, and a multitude is also a great throng.

clue.text: Purple, initially — red, sort of blue

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word purple

parts.note: Red was a common label for Soviet Russians

explanation.surface: A colour list: purple first, then red, then a type of blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a colour in a list of colours, but it means a communist, so a Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussian blue is a deep blue pigment named after the German state.

clue.text: Area some returned to provide the above opening

indicators.note: returned means the two pieces together are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: a rood is an old unit of land area, a quarter of an acre
some means a part

explanation.surface: A section of land is turned over to make an opening overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ROODPART round. A ROOD is an old British land measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapdoor is a hinged hatch set in a ceiling or floor, an opening overhead.

clue.text: Responsibility not borne by them, apparently

definitions.meaning: split as '...', the burden falls ... rather than on them

explanation.definitionFit: A burden of duty, and split in two it says the load is on ourselves and not on them.

clue.text: Exchange ideas and arrange score an' tempo?

indicators.note: arrange, set among musical words, tells us to rearrange the letters

parts.note: an' is a clipped spelling of and, giving the letters A and N

explanation.surface: Musicians share views on how to arrange the score and tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrange' reworks SCORE AN TEMPO; the musical surface tempts a reading about notes in a score.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare notes is the idiom for sharing opinions and experiences.

clue.text: Unofficially cancelled the best performance

parts.note: an event cancelled is off
the record is the best performance ever achieved

explanation.surface: A top performance quietly scrapped without any official word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said off the record is not for publication or attribution.

clue.text: Equivalent of sovereign, initially, in republic

definitions.meaning: the gold coin was first valued at twenty shillings, one pound, like a sovereign

explanation.walkthrough: The British coin later settled at 21 shillings, but at first it was worth 20, as a sovereign was.
explanation.definitionFit: The old gold coin was originally worth a pound like the sovereign, and the name is also a West African state.

clue.text: Gentlemen's murals make a fair gift

indicators.note: make here means the letters are put together into something new

explanation.surface: Drawings on the walls of a men's room count as a generous present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' reworks FAIR GIFT; 'Gentlemen's' is the gents' lavatory, whose walls attract scrawls.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti are scrawled writings and drawings, notoriously found on lavatory walls.

clue.text: Eccentric on prose

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, out of line, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A description of an oddball's way with words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' jumbles ON PROSE; the whole clue describes the Oxford don famous for transposing the starts of words.
explanation.definitionFit: William Spooner was an Oxford don noted for verbal slips that swapped sounds in phrases.

clue.text: Teachers or deputy head in market town

parts.note: a school's teachers are its staff

indicators.note: head means the opening letter of the word deputy

explanation.surface: A school's teachers or deputy head living in a country town.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFORD is the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is an English county town that has long held markets.

clue.text: Rage, in a way

definitions.meaning: a craze, as in 'all the rage'
a manner of doing something, as in 'after a ...'

explanation.definitionFit: A craze or trend is all the rage, and a manner or style of doing things is also a way.

clue.text: Appropriate postulate held by primate

indicators.note: held by means one word sits inside the word for primate

parts.note: an ape is a primate
to postulate is to posit

explanation.surface: A suitable theory proposed by a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite remarks are relevant and well suited to the occasion.

clue.text: Survey what TV addicts do

definitions.meaning: a general look at the whole
split as ..., they watch too much

explanation.definitionFit: A broad survey of a subject, and couch potatoes who view excessively.

clue.text: Little room for privacy, note, in the country

parts.note: a den is a small private room
to note is to mark

explanation.surface: A private snug and a memo found somewhere in the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian nation.

clue.text: Polishing material is carried back by an Indian

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: carried means the following letters are held inside the word for Indian

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior

indicators.note: back means the word is is read backwards

explanation.surface: A polishing product is transported home by a man from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS into SI, which is 'carried' inside BRAVE. 'Indian' suggests India but means a Native American brave.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasive is a gritty substance used to grind or polish surfaces.

clue.text: Under control, like quarterdeck ready for bridge inspection

definitions.text: like quarterdeck ready for bridge inspection
definitions.meaning: a quarter of a 52-card deck is the 13 cards a bridge player holds and looks at

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarterdeck' and 'bridge' suggest a ship, but this is cards: a quarter of the deck dealt for bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation being managed is in hand, and thirteen cards held for a bridge deal are a player's hand.

clue.text: Needlewoman's fall

definitions.meaning: a knitter who works a particular stitch

explanation.walkthrough: To 'come a purler' is British informal for falling heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitter who works purl stitches, and in British slang a heavy fall, as in 'came a cropper'.

clue.text: Accept responsibility, as conductors do

definitions.meaning: to take the consequences of one's actions
orchestra conductors stand looking at the scores

explanation.definitionFit: Taking one's punishment bravely, and literally what a conductor does, looking towards the scores.

clue.text: Musical craft

definitions.meaning: Andrew Lloyd Webber's stage show about felines
a cat or catboat is a kind of sailing boat

explanation.definitionFit: A long-running stage show about felines, and catamarans or catboats are vessels.

clue.text: Humming top follows circular curve

parts.note: a circle drawn is the shape O
a top is a lid

explanation.surface: A spinning top hums as it traces a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humming' looks like the noise of a spinning top but means smelly, a sense of the rare word OLID.
explanation.definitionFit: Olid is a rare word for stinking; to 'hum' is British slang for to smell bad.

clue.text: Hardy native, for example, about to join artist

parts.note: re means about, concerning
J M W Turner was an English painter

explanation.surface: A Hardy character joins up with a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy wrote 'The Return of the Native', so his native is one who comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's native comes home, so he is an example of someone coming back.

clue.text: Tower demolished to maintain control

parts.note: a keep is a castle's central tower
a building demolished is down

explanation.surface: A castle tower is knocked down to hold power.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep someone down is to hold them in check and suppress them.
